Insurance · regression assurance

Every rule change.
A traceable test story.

Rule2Test turns an insurance rule revision into reviewed regression tests and execution evidence you can hand to an auditor — with the AI never deciding pass or fail.

Every figure in this deck is copied from an artifact in the repository. Synthetic data; not production measurements.

The problem

A rule changes. Nobody can prove what it broke.

  • The boundary that moved is exactly the case the existing suite never covered.
  • Nobody can say which tests the change invalidated, or who accepted the new ones.
  • A green suite is presented as evidence, but nothing links a result back to the clause that caused it.
  • Reviewers are asked to trust an AI summary of a document they cannot re-check line by line.

The gap is not test generation. It is traceability and authority.

The moment

A passing suite was never the point.

We inject an off-by-one at the exact threshold that moved. The generated boundary test catches it, and the release gate flips to NO-GO with a concrete counterexample — an age, not a stack trace.

How it works

Five stages, one audit trail.

StageWhat happensWho decides
IngestTwo rule versions; source bytes archived and hashedDeterministic
AnalyzeRule delta, impact, bounded gap search, candidate testsDeterministic
ReviewExplicit, revision-bound approval per testHuman
ExecuteApproved tests only, against an independent system under testDeterministic
ProveEvidence pack plus a GO / NO-GO regression gateDeterministic

Each stage binds to a workflow revision. A stale action fails instead of silently overwriting work.

The differentiator

AI proposes. Engines decide. A human approves.

  • AI never computes expected. A typed oracle does, from the reviewed rules.
  • AI never sees the answer. Ground truth is compared only after the model returns.
  • Every extracted rule cites an exact source line. If the quote is not literally in the document, we reject the output.
  • No retry, no repair, no fallback to mock. A provider failure is classified and surfaced, never hidden.
  • Nothing is approved automatically — not rules, not tests, not the AI's own proposals.

Stage 2 · analyze

Find the cases nobody wrote.

16.67% → 100.0%designed boundary coverage, baseline to final
100.0%mutation score on the same synthetic scenario

Designed coverage on one synthetic scenario. Coverage is not a pass rate and not release approval.

Stage 3 · review

Approval is a person, a reason, and a revision.

Edit a test after approval and the approval is void. Reopening review clears approvals and invalidates the current GO context.

Stage 4 · execute

Expected and actual never share code.

The system under test receives inputs only — never the expected result and never the rule snapshot.

Stage 5 · prove

Evidence an auditor can re-verify.

SHA-256 detects corruption. It is an integrity check, not a digital signature, and it does not stop an administrator who rewrites both the payload and the hash.

Engineering

Built to be debugged on stage.

275 passingautomated tests, standard library core
11provider failure kinds, each with a remediation hint
0automatic retries, fallbacks or auto-approvals

Logs use a field allowlist, so document text, prompts, reviewer names and session tokens cannot reach a log line. Counters are process-local and reset on restart.

Scope

What we do not claim.

  • Not a general insurance reasoning engine — the supported rule DSL is deliberately small and rejects what it cannot express.
  • Not production-ready: reviewer names are self-declared; there is no authentication, RBAC or deployment hardening.
  • Not a release authorization — GO is a local regression assessment for one workflow revision.
  • Not measured: reviewer acceptance, effort savings, production accuracy, token cost, SME-reviewed labels.
  • Synthetic results throughout. Mock providers are labelled simulated everywhere they appear.

We would rather be trusted on five numbers than doubted on fifty.

Next

From a demo to a pipeline.

  • Evaluate real extraction and embedding models against a broader, SME-labelled corpus.
  • Richer decision-table analysis and metamorphic tests beyond single-field boundaries.
  • Integrate a real system under test through the existing HTTP adapter.
  • Authenticated roles, signed evidence, append-only audit storage and operational monitoring.

Every rule change becomes test coverage and auditable evidence.
